run: B0 — go/no-go gate for Paper B (compositional-OOD WM abstraction)
box: vast.ai ssh9 RTX 5070 Ti 16GB Blackwell sm_120, driver 580.95.05

blackwell_torch.note: cu128 wheel imports + runs GPU matmul on Blackwell with no 'no kernel image' error. mani-skill 3.0.1, sapien 3.0.3 work on it.

task.object_count_knob: env kwarg num_cubes (int>=1); adds num_cubes-1 inert distractor cubes to the STATE obs
task.why: PickCubeMulti (pick+lift to floating goal) was NOT learnable in budget (grasp 91% but place ~0%, succ ~0 even at N=1). Switched to PushCube core which is learnable.

precondition_1_beats_random.method: official ManiSkill PPO (ppo.py, state obs), PushCubeMulti N=2, 4M steps, num_envs=1024
precondition_1_beats_random.verdict: PASS — PPO clearly beats random (1.0 vs 0.0 success; 35.7 vs 3.1 return)
precondition_1_beats_random.caveat: My from-scratch PPO was buggy (PushCube floored at 0 succ); official ppo.py solves it -> used official.

precondition_2_value_decode_collapse.method: linear ridge probe: flat state -> discounted return-to-go (gamma=0.8); 25600 samples; 80/20 CV, 3 seeds
precondition_2_value_decode_collapse.verdict: FAIL — value-decodability is essentially FLAT (~0.46-0.52) across object counts. No collapse: changes (~0.03) are within-noise and same magnitude for random vs trained policy. Inert distractors create no compositional value interaction.

verdict_reasoning: Precondition 1 (control signal) PASSES strongly. Precondition 2 (compositional headroom) FAILS: passive distractor objects do not change the target task's value structure, so a linear probe decodes value equally well at held-out object counts, and the policy keeps solving the task OOD. Per pre-registration (GO iff BOTH), this is NO-GO. Honest read: this multi-object construction has no compositional-OOD headroom; a task where objects INTERACT with the value (must-avoid / count-dependent goal / relational objective) would be needed before a WM build. Designing such a task to force the signal risks the same procedure-trick critique as the TD-MPC-Glass pivot.
caveats: Distractors are physically inert and spatially separated -> by design they do not affect the push reward; this is exactly why no headroom appeared.
Probe uses return-to-go as the value target (model-free); a learned WM latent value could differ, but the linear-decodability-of-return result is the standard headroom proxy and it is flat.
OOD rollouts feed the N=2 policy its first 45 (target-relevant) obs dims; the policy is dim-agnostic to extra distractors by construction, hence OOD success stays ~0.99.
